subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu support automatic group-sender agent provisioning, and what identity, authorization, quota/lifecycle, and shared/private memory boundaries should become the public contract?
rationale: The request changes durable agent creation, workspace/config mutation, memory isolation, routing authority, and cost/security boundaries rather than only fixing a Feishu session-key bug.

options.title: Design Generic Contract First
options.body: Approve a generic, admin-authorized identity-to-agent lifecycle and shared/private memory contract, then implement Feishu as one channel/plugin adopter.

options.title: Keep Explicit Routing Only
options.body: Keep current group session scoping plus explicit thread-bound subagents and document external deployment patterns for per-user agent fleets.

options.title: Decline Automatic Provisioning
options.body: Close this direction if group chat sender identities should not automatically create durable agents inside OpenClaw.

recommendation.title: Design Generic Contract First
recommendation.body: Approve a generic, admin-authorized identity-to-agent lifecycle and shared/private memory contract, then implement Feishu as one channel/plugin adopter.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans Feishu routing, plugin API boundaries, subagent semantics, memory/security policy, and core-lean product direction where recent history points to this person as the strongest routing candidate.
